Fixed. The problem wasn't the button's base style — it was that the button boots in the keyboard-selected state, and "selected" swapped the fill to `--color-purple-bright`, dropping the white text to ~2.9:1 contrast. What you were looking at was the worst state of the button, permanently.

The change in [style.css:249](src/style.css:249): selection no longer lightens the fill. The background stays `--color-purple` (and the label is now pure white, which takes the resting contrast from 4.3:1 to ~5:1, passing AA), and the "you are here" cue moved to the frame instead — a 1px teal outline with a soft teal glow, matching the accent language of the corner brackets and the ghost button next to it. `:active` still dips to the darker purple for press feedback.

Verified in the preview after a reload: computed styles show the purple fill, white text, and teal outline on the selected button, and the screenshot reads clearly — arguably the selection cue is more arcade-y than the old brightness swap anyway. Hovering gets the same treatment, so there's no state left where the label sits on light purple.
